purpose: Checkout responses no longer wait for the payments provider; authorisation happens after the response, driven by a worker.

essential_concepts.name: Asynchronous completion
essential_concepts.description: A successful checkout response now means the order was accepted and recorded, not that payment was authorised. Completion happens later, out of band.

essential_concepts.name: Outbox record as the handoff
essential_concepts.description: The handler and the worker communicate through a row in the outbox table written in the same operation as the order, rather than through an in-process call.

essential_behavior_changes.name: Authorisation leaves the request path
essential_behavior_changes.description: OrderService.Create no longer calls the payments client. It writes the order and an outbox entry and returns.

essential_behavior_changes.name: Orders gain a lifecycle state
essential_behavior_changes.description: Orders are created as 'pending' and become 'authorized' or 'failed' once the worker has run, so the order's state now moves over time.

essential_behavior_changes.name: Failures surface later
essential_behavior_changes.description: A declined payment no longer fails the HTTP request; it leaves the order in the failed state and the caller must observe that separately.

important_components.name: OrderService
important_components.description: Creates orders. Changed: it now records an outbox entry instead of authorising payment inline.

important_components.name: Outbox store
important_components.description: New. Persists pending work alongside the order so nothing is lost between the two execution contexts.

important_components.name: Completion worker
important_components.description: New. Claims outbox entries, calls the payments client and updates the order state.

important_components.name: Payments client
important_components.description: Unchanged, but now called from the worker rather than from the request path.

important_relationships.name: OrderService writes to the outbox
important_relationships.description: The service inserts the order and the outbox entry together.

important_relationships.name: Worker reads the outbox and calls payments
important_relationships.description: The worker polls for pending entries and drives authorisation.

important_flows.name: Checkout
important_flows.description: POST /orders -> OrderService.Create -> order and outbox rows written -> response returned -> worker claims the entry -> payments authorisation -> order state updated.

before_state: POST /orders authorised payment inside the request. The response was only successful if the provider accepted the payment, and a slow provider slowed the request.
after_state: POST /orders persists a pending order plus an outbox entry and returns immediately. A separate worker process authorises payment and moves the order to authorized or failed.

supporting_context.name: The worker is a separate entry point
supporting_context.description: cmd/worker is a new binary, so the deployment now runs two processes.

supporting_context.name: Retry behaviour
supporting_context.description: Entries that fail are left for the next poll rather than retried immediately.

incidental.name: The go.mod and README edits
incidental.description: Housekeeping that carries no behavioural meaning.
